configurePresets.name: windows-clang-cl-base
configurePresets.description: The Windows lane: clang-cl + Ninja through cmake/windows-clang-cl.toolchain.cmake (the engine's clang-cl shim as the compiler launcher, vcpkg chain-loaded: SDL2 + FFmpeg from vcpkg.json; VCPKG_ROOT must point at a vcpkg checkout). Windows hosts only -- on macOS/Linux these presets do not exist (`cmake --list-presets` shows none) and the plain configure in README is the build. Nothing here touches the macOS/Linux defaults.

configurePresets.name: windows-clang-cl-release
configurePresets.description: The shipped Windows shape: Release, the vcpkg DLLs beside twinsanityevolved.exe (tools/ci/release_dist.ps1 -SkipBuild -BuildDir build-windows-release stages it). The CI job .github/workflows/windows.yml builds this preset.

configurePresets.name: windows-clang-cl-dev
configurePresets.description: The development configuration: optimised code with PDBs (crash dumps and a debugger read the frames; the 39 MB of wasm2c C is impractical at /Od), the same dependencies as the release preset.

configurePresets.name: windows-clang-cl-release-lto
configurePresets.displayName: Windows release + LTO (clang-cl, lld-link, Ninja, Release)
configurePresets.description: windows-clang-cl-release with TE_LTO=ON (CMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION here and PS2R_LTO on the engine, through CheckIPOSupported) and lld-link as the linker (link.exe does not read clang-cl's LTO objects). Not the shipped shape until it passes the unit tests, a boot and a save-state round trip on a Windows machine -- the engine's windows-release-lto has the same status.

configurePresets.name: vita-base
configurePresets.description: The PS Vita lane's common settings: cmake/vita.toolchain.cmake wraps $VITASDK/share/vita.toolchain.cmake and the eboot's C/C++ is cross-compiled (TE_VITA=ON in CMakeLists.txt: the renderer on vitaGL, SDL2's Vita port for pads and audio, FFmpeg cross-compiled by tools/vita/ffmpeg_vita.sh, the disc image read from ux0:data/twinsanity/). Builds twinsanityevolved.vpk with the shipped shader set (tools/vita/shader_seed). Nothing here touches the macOS / Linux / Windows configurations (every Vita difference sits under if(TE_VITA)).

configurePresets.name: vita-release
configurePresets.description: The PS Vita package, the release's one (.github/workflows/release.yml): the game's code compiled natively for the console's ARM processor by the Vita's GCC (TE_VITA_NATIVE=ON: tools/te_cxx_arm.py, cmake/native_lane.cmake); the retail address space is a 32 MB block in the eboot (runner/te_native.h).

configurePresets.name: vita-module-release
configurePresets.displayName: PlayStation Vita, the game as the wasm2c module (A/B against vita-release)
configurePresets.description: The earlier PS Vita build, for a developer's A/B against vita-release: the game's code compiled to wasm32 by the pinned toolchain (tools/fetch_toolchain.sh) and lowered to C by wasm2c, as on the desktop (TE_VITA_NATIVE=OFF). Its own build directory. README.md's PS Vita section has the Vita3K recipe that compares the two.
